newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on Chinese demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on Chinese demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed late afteroon on Monday in active trading as players expected a new wave of buying from China to support to the market, traders said.
"China is still looking for January cargoes and they are also buying cargoes for February," one trader said.
January gas oil swaps traded several times at between $31.09 and $32.22 per barrel, brokers said.
The market was last quoted unchanged at $32.20/$32.30 a barrel, up from midday's $32.05/$32.15, one broker said.
One trader said market talk of Chinese January imports at par to December's estimated 800,000-tonnes, has led to firmer prices.
"There are reports that China may allow imports without any duty for January or the first quarter," a trader said.
The January/February time spread traded at an unchanged $1.05 a barrel, a broker said.
Jet fuel also edged up on demand from North Asia for the winter and prompt supplies are tight within the region traders said.
The January jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was last quoted at $2.20/$2.40 per barrel, up from Friday's $2.00/$2.50, a broker said.
The February regrade was also quoted slightly firmer with bids seen at $1.85/$2.10 from Friday's $1.80/$1.90 per barrel.
The market was also boosted by the issue of purchase tenders by several countries for both jet fuel and gas oil, including India, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
Traders said the emergence of buying from Indonesia for jet fuel has added to the bullish sentiment.
Both fuel oil and naphtha quotes were steady in quiet trade, brokers said.
January fuel oil was quoted at $121.25/$122.25 per tonne and January naphtha was notionally indicated at $24.50/$24.65 a barrel.
